anti_overlap: fd-spice-blending-flavor-axes covers axis independence; this covers how axes combine in an ensemble context
decision_lens: Ensemble texture from individual variation — each voice must be distinct enough to hear but similar enough to blend
distance_rationale: Gamelan tuning is a musical practice about creating ensemble texture from deliberate individual variation — a direct structural parallel to personality variety in a colony.
expected_isomorphisms: Paired tuning maps to complementary personality pairings. Stratification maps to temporal scales of personality expression. Embat (unequal intervals) maps to non-linear behavioral mappings. Pathet (modal emphasis) maps to situational axis foregrounding.
focus: How Javanese gamelan tuning creates distinct instrument voices that interlock into ensemble texture
name: fd-gamelan-tuning-ensemble
persona: Javanese gamelan tuner (penyelaras) who tunes each instrument in an ensemble to its own unique pitch set, creating a shimmering texture from deliberate micro-differences between instruments
review_areas: Evaluate the 'paired tuning' principle: gamelan instruments come in pairs tuned slightly apart to create beating patterns. Should personality pairs in the colony create similar 'beating' dynamics — not identical, not clashing, but productively different?

Check whether the system supports 'stratification' — gamelan music has elaboration layers where different instruments play the same melody at different speeds. Do personality axes operate at different temporal scales (introversion=constant, patience=situational, pride=reactive)?

Assess the 'embat' question: gamelan tuning is NOT equal temperament — intervals are deliberately unequal to create the ensemble's unique character. Should personality axes have non-linear behavioral mappings rather than linear 0.0-1.0?

Evaluate whether a colony of elves produces 'shimmer' — the gamelan term for the acoustic effect of slight differences. A colony should shimmer with personality variation, not clang with opposition or drone with sameness

Check for the 'pathet' principle: gamelan pieces operate in modes that foreground certain pitches and background others. Do different game situations (revel, workshop, conflict) foreground different personality axes?

severity_examples.condition: Every system uses all 3 axes with equal weight
severity_examples.scenario: All personality axes are equally salient in all situations — no 'modal' foregrounding means the player can't learn which axis matters when

severity_examples.condition: All behavioral effects scale linearly with axis value
severity_examples.scenario: Linear 0.0-1.0 mapping means the behavioral difference between 0.3 and 0.4 is the same as between 0.8 and 0.9 — no interesting non-linearity at the extremes

source_domain: Javanese gamelan tuning and ensemble design (karawitan)
success_hints: Personality creates an ensemble 'shimmer' — each elf is distinct but they blend into a cohesive colony character. Different game situations naturally foreground different axes.
task_context: The game is an ensemble simulation where 8-20 characters interact. Gamelan has centuries of wisdom about how individual voices combine into ensemble texture.
